function: Excluded, system (p. 3): over-the-air FL aggregation (area 7) with a scalar uplink model, i.e. single-antenna edge and central UAVs, and no RIS.
notes: PDF matches the DOI: title and DOI 10.1109/TVT.2024.3461650 on p. 1 (IEEE TVT correspondence, published version). Checks 1 to 5 pass: it proposes and simulates a method, and its FL aggregates over the air, p. 3: "we consider an analog AirComp scheme for achieving model aggregation", with a misaligned-AirComp MLE estimator as a stated contribution (p. 1), so area 7 by function; nothing learned controls resources, power or beams, so it is not area 6. Check 6 applies to this area-7 work because the link is single-antenna at both ends with no RIS: p. 2, Eq. (2) gives a scalar LoS channel power gain h_k(t) = beta0 d^-2; p. 3, Eqs. (3)-(4) give a scalar precoding factor alpha_k = 1/(estimated channel coefficient) and a scalar received signal r(t) = sum_k h_k x_k(t - tau_k) + z(t). Fig. 1(a) (p. 2) and Table II (p. 4) give no antenna count and no RIS (the 2 GHz and 1 GHz of Table II are CPU frequencies). For the reviewer: the links are UAV to UAV (aerial). I read "OTFS and NTN works admit single-antenna links" as the works of areas 4 and 6, and the precedence of 7 over 6 keeps this work in area 7. If that exemption is meant to cover any aerial link, the work would be included as area 7 with provisional marks q1 0 (custom free-space A2A model, p. 2), q2 0 (the sweep over 3 to 15 UAVs measures training with each number, no train-test mismatch stated, p. 4), q3 likely 0 (baselines are two own ablations, aligned AirComp [13] and FedAvg [19], no non-learned method, p. 4), q4 1 (p. 4: "O(K 2 log(K))"), q5 0 (COCO is a task dataset, no code or channel data released, p. 4).
